title: Why Going 10x Is Psychologically Easier Than Going 2x
alt_title_1: The Counterintuitive Math Behind '10x Is Easier Than 2x'
alt_title_2: Why Doubling Your Output Causes Burnout (While 10x Simplifies)
description_hook: Aiming for 2x tricks you into keeping 80% low-value busywork and working longer nights. Dan Sullivan and Dr. Benjamin Hardy show why a 10x lens forces ruthless simplicity around your 20% asymmetric core.

scenes.headline: Why 2x Ambition Breeds Exhaustion
bullets: Most people assume bigger targets require 10x more hours
In practice, moderate targets trap you inside broken routines
scenes.narration: Aiming for ten-times growth sounds ten times harder than doubling your current output. Psychologically, the exact opposite is true.
scenes.source: Dan Sullivan & Benjamin Hardy, 10x Is Easier Than 2x (2023)

scenes.headline: Sullivan & Hardy's 10x Filter
scenes.stat_label: DAILY BUSYWORK KEPT ALIVE BY 2X GOALS
bullets: You can brute-force 2x growth by sacrificing sleep and weekends
Brute force never forces you to question low-value habits
scenes.narration: Strategist Dan Sullivan and psychologist Benjamin Hardy explain why in 10x Is Easier Than 2x. Chasing two-x growth tricks you into keeping your current habits and simply grinding twice as long.
scenes.source: Dan Sullivan & Benjamin Hardy, 10x Is Easier Than 2x (2023)

scenes.headline: Linear Brute Force vs Asymmetric Pruning
scenes.left_body: Keep 80% busywork -> work 2x longer -> hit a ceiling
scenes.right_body: Cut 80% noise -> go all-in on 20% compounding core
scenes.narration: A two-x target lets eighty percent of your daily busywork survive. A ten-x target makes brute force impossible, forcing you to drop everything except the twenty percent asymmetric core.
scenes.source: Dan Sullivan & Benjamin Hardy, 10x Is Easier Than 2x (2023)

scenes.headline: Run the Sunday 20% Core Audit
scenes.stat_subtext: Subtract 4 of 5 low-return tasks -> compound quality
scenes.narration: Apply the Ten-X Filter every Sunday: identify the narrow twenty percent of work producing nearly all real leverage, and ruthlessly eliminate or automate the noisy eighty percent.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)

scenes.headline: Subtract Noise Before Adding Effort
bullets: Stop asking how to squeeze more tasks into your calendar
Ask which 4 tasks vanish when you raise the standard
scenes.narration: Doubling traps you in linear hustle; ten-x forces radical simplicity. That hidden shift explains why...
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
